sources.title: Favorable Antiviral Effect of Metformin on SARS-CoV-2 Viral Load in a Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial of COVID-19
sources.design: Randomized placebo-controlled trial; virologic companion analysis
sources.population: Adults with acute COVID-19 in the COVID-OUT trial
sources.preview: Metformin reduced nasal SARS-CoV-2 RNA during acute infection. This virologic analysis uses participants from COVID-OUT.

sources.title: Metformin Prevents Dopaminergic Neuron Death in MPTP/P-Induced Mouse Model of Parkinson’s Disease via Autophagy and Mitochondrial ROS Clearance
sources.population: MPTP/probenecid mouse model and cultured cells
sources.preview: Experiments examined autophagy, mitochondrial oxidative stress and dopamine-producing nerve cells in models of Parkinson’s disease.

sources.title: Metformin blunts muscle hypertrophy in response to progressive resistance exercise training in older adults: The MASTERS trial
sources.population: Healthy adults aged 65 years and older undergoing resistance training
sources.preview: Metformin attenuated gains in lean and thigh muscle mass during resistance training; differences in strength gains were not statistically significant.

sources.title: Metformin improves cognitive impairment in patients with schizophrenia: associated with enhanced functional connectivity of dorsolateral prefrontal cortex
sources.population: Clinically stable schizophrenia of at most five years duration; young adults at the Second Xiangya Hospital, China; mean age 22.8 years.
sources.preview: Adjunctive metformin improved the reported composite cognitive-test score over 24 weeks in this small open-label trial.

Results: Metformin ameliorated cognitive dysfunction as evaluated by the MCCB; Figure 2

sources.sampleDescription: 72 randomized: metformin plus antipsychotics 48, antipsychotics alone 24. 59 completed 24 weeks. Completion is not the model-analysis denominator.
sources.intervention: Metformin 500 mg three times daily added to antipsychotics for 24 weeks

sources.title: Metformin and physical performance in older people with probable sarcopenia and physical prefrailty or frailty in England (MET-PREVENT): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial
sources.population: Adults 65 years or older with probable sarcopenia, slow 4-m walking speed and physical prefrailty or frailty; Gateshead and Newcastle, England; mean age 80.4 years.
sources.preview: Metformin did not improve four-metre walking speed after four months and was poorly tolerated in this older frail population.
